subject: SLO calibration & harness alignment — proposed measurement definitions and run window
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@asterlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-20T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: SLO calibration & harness alignment — proposed measurement definitions and run window

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the concrete asks we discussed so we can get a reproducible qualification run scheduled.

Recap (high level)
- Goal: validate that Redwood meets Aster Labs' interactive streaming SLOs under your expected traffic profile (chat-style assistance embedded in checkout flow).
- Primary SLOs you called out: fast first-token delivery for streaming and stable tail latencies under promotional peaks.
- We proposed a two-phase qualification: 1) calibration runs to align measurement definitions and harness parameters, 2) full stress/soak runs across target concurrency points.

What we need from you to configure the harness
- Representative prompt set (we attached a small sample: aster_prompt_samples-2028.jsonl) — please confirm that the included intents map to your production mix (checkout help, price-matching, order-status).
- Expected traffic profile: sustained QPS and peak concurrent streaming sessions (see questions below).
- Which latency numbers matter to your SLAs: first-token p95/p99, end-to-end p95/p99, or both?

Suggested measurement definitions (draft — please confirm)
- first_token_latency: time from Redwood receiving the HTTP request to first token byte emitted by the server (server-side measurement). We will also capture client-observed TTFB (end-to-end).
- full_response_latency: time from request->final token emitted. For streaming we report inter-token latency distribution as well.
- effective_throughput: tokens/sec aggregated across all streams; request_success_rate excludes transient 429/5xx.

Calibration parameters we plan to vary
- Concurrency sweep: [50, 150, 300, 600] concurrent streaming sessions
- Per-stream token rate: 3–8 tokens/sec (configurable per test)
- Prompt length buckets: short (<=40 tokens), medium (40–150), long (>150)
- Model pinned for runs: redwood/open-1.0-quant (exact hash in harness spec)

Proposed next steps
1) You confirm the prompt set and traffic numbers (sustained QPS, expected peak concurrency) — reply inline.
2) We run a 30-minute calibration on Wed 2028-04-26 09:00 PT to validate measurement alignment and collect baseline telemetry.
3) After calibration, we schedule two stress windows for throughput and tail-latency characterization.

Attachments: harness-spec-v1.3.md (harness commands + measurement hooks), aster_prompt_samples-2028.jsonl (10 representative prompts).

Thanks — attaching a short checklist in the harness doc. If Wednesday won’t work, propose another morning slot.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com

From: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@asterlabs.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Cho <kevin.cho@asterlabs.com>
Date: 2028-04-20T12:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO calibration & harness alignment — proposed measurement definitions and run window

Thanks Mateo — this is a helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side inline below.

Traffic profile (prod baseline)
- Sustained: ~220 requests/sec during normal hours (checkout microservice).
- Promo peaks: historically up to ~1,800 short-lived concurrent sessions (we realize this is high — most are sub-60s). For qualification we can focus on the sustained->peak sweep and a separate short-burst test.
- Streaming behavior: chat sessions stream 1st token asap then stream a few tokens intermittently; average per-session token rate ~5 tokens/sec during active typing.

SLO priorities
- First-token p95 <= 200 ms (client-observed TTFB ideally < 250 ms).
- First-token p99 <= 450 ms only during sustained loads; for promo bursts we care more about graceful degradation (no hard errors, predictable retry guidance).
- Full response p95 target is softer: <= 1.2s for medium prompts.

Measurement questions
- When you say first_token_latency (server-side) — do you measure before or after any edge/CDN? We need both server-side and client-observed numbers to understand network contributions.
- Can the harness replay be configured to include a lightweight CDN emulation (extra 10–60 ms RTT) so we get nearer to prod-ish numbers?

We can commit to providing anonymized request traces and a small sample of production logs by EOD 2028-04-24 (we'll scrub PII). Kevin — can you confirm?

Wed 4/26 09:00 PT works for a calibration run on our side. Also please include a short checklist of the data you need in advance (time sync, IP allowlist, DSP for temporary dedicated capacity).

— Samantha
Samantha Nguyen
Head of Integrations, Aster Labs
samantha.nguyen@asterlabs.com

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@asterlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-21T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO calibration & harness alignment — proposed measurement definitions and run window

Samantha — thanks for the quick detail. Short answers and actions below.

1) Server-side vs client-observed metrics
- We'll collect both. Server-side first_token_latency = time from arrival at the Redwood front-end to first token emitted by model runtime (no CDN). Client-observed TTFB = measured by our test client (which can include an artificial latency element to emulate CDN). We'll report both numbers side-by-side and provide a delta so you can attribute network overhead.

2) CDN emulation / network shaping
- Yes — harness supports an optional network-shaping layer. For calibration we suggest adding a 20–50 ms RTT with 1–2% packet jitter to emulate your edge. We'll add a flag in harness-spec-v1.3.md (see section 2.2).

3) Calibration plan (concrete)
- Wed 2028-04-26 09:00 PT: 30-minute run, concurrency points [50, 150, 300], with CDN emulation at 30 ms RTT. Goal: validate measurement hooks and ensure logs align.
- Thu 2028-04-27 11:00 PT: extended stress window (soak) covering sustained 220 RPS and a 10-minute burst to 600 concurrent streams.

4) Measurement definitions (finalized for the harness)
- first_token_server_us: microseconds from request accept -> first token out (server only).
- first_token_client_ms: measured by client harness (includes emulated RTT).
- inter_token_ms_dist: distribution of intervals between tokens for streaming responses.
- success_rate_percent: % of requests returning 2xx within configured timeout.
- p95/p99 computed over 5-minute rolling windows and reported per-concurrency bucket.

5) Data / infra checklist (what we need from Aster)
- Time sync: confirm NTP sync within 100 ms for any client-side collectors.
- IP allowlist: we'll provide a short list of test IPs for the calibration run; please confirm ACL window.
- Temporary capacity: if you want dedicated capacity for the burst window, we'll need a request by 2028-04-24 — Marissa will own the infra approval.

Next actions assigned
- Mateo: finalize harness flags and add CDN emulation example (by EOD 4/21).
- Marissa: open dedicated-capacity request and provide escalation path.
- Samantha / Kevin: share anonymized logs by 4/24.

I've attached an updated harness snippet and the prompt pack. Let me know if you want the calibration run earlier.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
